papers_read.title_as_printed: TASNet: A tri-modal attentive scale robust adaptive fusion framework for progressive mild cognitive impairment classification (Zhu et al., Journal of Neuroscience Methods 430 (2026) 110726)
An end-to-end multimodal 3D CNN framework with multi-level features for the prediction of mild cognitive impairment (Zhang, He, Liu, Ong, Liu, Teng; Knowledge-Based Systems 281 (2023) 111064)

what_each_reports.P-23: Tri-modal sMRI + FDG-PET + CSF TASNet, ADNI1/2, single 8:1:1 split. sMCI vs pMCI (36-month criterion, 200 MCI, about 20 test subjects): accuracy 85.00%, AUC 91.67%. AD vs CN (352 subjects, 36 test): accuracy 94.44%, AUC 97.52% (Table 5).
what_each_reports.P-72: Twin 3D ResNet18 with attention and spatial pyramid pooling on sMRI grey-matter maps + FDG-PET, ADNI (215 AD, 246 NC, 151 pMCI, 238 sMCI; pMCI = conversion within 3 years), 70/15/15 subject-level split repeated over three test subsets. AD vs NC: accuracy 94.61% (0.85), AUC 0.947. sMCI vs pMCI: accuracy 77.19% (1.01), AUC 0.755 (Table 5). Five-fold CV on a fixed subset: 93.83% and 77.19%.

quantity_a: As recorded: P-23 pMCI vs sMCI accuracy (T2, 36-month horizon, tri-modal input, about 20 test subjects).
quantity_b: As recorded: 94.61%, which in P-72 is AD vs NC diagnostic accuracy, not a T2 conversion result. P-72's T2 figure is 77.19% (sMRI+PET, 3-year horizon).
incompatible_if_same: No on either like-for-like reading. AD vs CN: P-23 94.44% vs P-72 94.61%, essentially identical. sMCI vs pMCI: P-23 85.00% (about 17 of 20 test subjects, Wilson 95% interval roughly 64-95%) vs P-72 77.19%; the interval contains 77.19%, and P-23 adds CSF biomarkers that P-72 does not use.

gates.task: mismatch as recorded (T2 conversion vs AD-vs-NC diagnosis); match (T2) only if P-72's 77.19% is substituted.
gates.validation_tier: match in tier (internal splits only); P-23 one small split, P-72 averaged over three splits plus a five-fold check.
gates.modality_family: partial mismatch: both combine structural MRI with FDG-PET, but P-23 also uses CSF fluid biomarkers; neither is 'structural_mri' only as the record states.

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible as recorded (conversion endpoint vs AD-vs-NC diagnosis); both are accuracy.
performance_validity: flag does not apply: 94.61% (P-72) and 94.44%/85.00% (P-23) accuracies are below 0.97; P-23's AD vs CN AUC 97.52% on 36 test subjects would trip the test but is not the contested figure.
independence: Distinct studies and author groups; both use ADNI imaging, so participant overlap is possible.
grounds: The record misreads P-72: its 94.61% is AD vs NC accuracy, while P-72's sMCI vs pMCI accuracy is 77.19%.
On the matching AD vs CN comparison the two papers agree (94.44% vs 94.61%).
On the matching T2 comparison P-23's 85.00% rests on about 20 test subjects and cannot exclude 77.19%, and its input adds CSF biomarkers absent from P-72.
Neither paper claims an ordering the other refutes; there is no disagreement to adjudicate.

evidence_quotes.quote: Especially in AD diagnosis achieved an average accuracy of 94.61 %
The best accuracy was achieved in both prediction of AD vs. NC with 94.61 % and sMCI vs. pMCI with 77.19 % respectively
MCI subjects who developed AD within 3 years were labeled as pMCI and those who did not convert to AD were labeled as sMCI.
We followed the same data split strategy to construct three different subsets with different test sets, the average of three classification accuracies is used as the final result.
sMCI vs. pMCI: In this critical task for early prognosis, TASNet achieved 85.00% Accuracy and 86.96% F1 (Table 3)
AD vs. CN: In this baseline task (Table 5), TASNet achieved 94.44% Accuracy and 100.00% Sensitivity
selecting subjects from ADNI1 and ADNI2 cohorts with baseline T1-weighted sMRI, FDG-PET, and CSF biomarkers (Abeta42, TAU, PTAU).

record_defects: claim_b '94.61% AD on T2' is P-72's AD vs NC accuracy; P-72's T2 (sMCI vs pMCI) accuracy is 77.19%. task_equal 'Yes' is therefore wrong as recorded.
modality_family 'structural_mri' is wrong for both papers: P-72 fuses sMRI grey matter with FDG-PET; P-23 fuses sMRI, FDG-PET and CSF.
The rejection reason 'Metric type unclear: Acc / Unknown' is wrong: P-72's 94.61% is plainly an accuracy.
The bridging-evidence list names no separating condition and mixes metric types; 'partially resolved' is unsupported.
what_would_change_the_verdict: Nothing in these two papers: the like-for-like comparisons agree (AD vs CN) or overlap (T2). A larger P-23 test set whose T2 interval excluded 77.19% would still differ in predictor set (CSF), making it incommensurable rather than genuine.
